posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: A LETTER TO MUHSD | 209connect Newsletter — Read Aloud
posts.caption:
209connect Newsletter — Read Aloud | November 25, 2025

"Illegally Fired: A Letter to MUHSD." I forced disclosure, and now they are being legally forced to respond.

In this read-aloud edition of the 209connect Newsletter, David Sicairos reads the letter he sent to Brett Nickelson, Rebecca Shelton, and Superintendent Peterson of the Merced Union High School District (MUHSD) — about his public records request, the District's determination response, and its pattern of delay. The records are due December 19, 2025.

THE FULL LETTER:

To Brett Nickelson, Rebecca Shelton, and Superintendent Peterson. Regarding determination response, pattern of delay.

Mr. Nickelson, I am in receipt of your determination letter dated today. This is simply an acknowledgement that we have received your letter further delaying the release of records to now December 19, 2025, after a 14 day extension. I must also note, that after ignoring my first two simple requests, you intelligently acknowledged my final legal request for public information. And in each of those instances, the legal deadlines were barely met. One even seemed to be scheduled on a district holiday day off.

While I acknowledge your production of the personnel file, I note with significant concern your request to delay the production of electronic communications, Request number 5, until December 19, 2025. This represents a substantial delay beyond the statutory timeframe, particularly given that electronic records are easily searchable and retrievable.

It also does not escape my notice that the District is using the exact same playbook as August 2023. Back then, as confirmed by Ms. Fonseca's email on August 28, 2023, I was removed simply for sending emails to Superintendent Peterson regarding Substitute Pay Equity, clearly documented in the paperwork you just now sent.

In 2023, I chalked it up as miscommunication. I let this slide. In 2025, I am demanding one because things have became clear to me.

You cited Deliberative Process Privilege. Be advised: discussing how to silence an employee for advocating for fair pay in 2023, or exercising free speech in 2025, is not a deliberation, it is actually a liability.

Furthermore, your letter cites the Deliberative Process Privilege, Government Code, section seventy-nine twenty-seven point seven-oh-five, as a potential basis for withholding these records.

Let this email serve as notice: the public interest in disclosing whether a public agency yielded to external political pressure and doxing campaigns to terminate an employee far outweighs the District's interest in keeping those deliberations secret. Deliberative Process cannot be used to shield the District from accountability regarding potential violations of First Amendment rights or discriminatory practices.

I expect the records to be produced on or before December 19, 2025, with minimal redactions. I will be scrutinizing the exemption log closely. I look forward to receiving the unredacted communications. The clock is ticking.

Yours truly, David Sicairos, Office of the Sovereign Architect.

That letter went out November 25th, 2025. The records were due December 19th. This is 209connect, the newsletter, read aloud. The full letter is in the show notes, and the next edition is coming.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: Boring Works
posts.caption:
Hard seasons do not need heroic training. They need boring training.

Walk every day, lift on schedule, sleep like it matters, and repeat it next week. Boring works because boring repeats. The win is how many days you keep the promise. General info only.

More in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: One Money Check
posts.caption:
After a career break, money feels foggy. One money check clears it.

Once a week, fifteen minutes: write what came in, write what went out, and sort every dollar into keep, cut, or question. No shame in the list. No fixing everything at once. One check, once a week.

More systems in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: Papered Over
posts.caption:
When a decision is hard to defend, the file gets thicker.

A new label appears, the same paper gets filed again, and only the cover changes. That is how a decision gets papered over. Read past the label, compare the dates, and ask why the same paper needed a new name.

Full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: The Next Room
posts.caption: The next room matters more than the last one. After a firing, you do not win the next room by relitigating the old one. Own your numbers, say the hard thing plainly, and keep the promise you made to yourself. A ledger is not revenge. It is a record. Full lesson in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: TRAIN THROUGH IT
posts.caption:
TRAIN THROUGH IT.

A hard season does not cancel training. It changes the plan. Short walks, basic barbell work, and sleep you protect like part of the program. This is general information only, not medical advice, and never a promise about results. On the worst weeks, the win is showing up at all. Keep the routine boring, keep the load honest, and let consistency carry what motivation cannot.

General information only, not medical advice. Follow Elevated209 CBD.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: The Letter With No Reason
posts.caption:
The letter gives no reason.

September 18, one page ends a career, and the file names no warning and no process. September 11 brought the public post. Seven days later came the firing. The gap is not a verdict. It is the question the records still have to answer.

Full record in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: The System Angle
posts.caption:
THE SYSTEM ANGLE.

Institutions rarely say they are burying a decision. They slow it down, they rename it, and they file it where nobody looks. The timeline tells the story anyway. A public post, then a firing, then a letter with no reason attached. When the paper trail goes quiet, that quiet is itself a fact worth naming. Not proof of motive, but a gap the public deserves to see in daylight.

How institutions paper over a decision, document-grounded. Follow @castlecaliforniacounterintel.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: Atwater Angle
posts.caption:
ATWATER ANGLE.

A district decision does not stay inside a boardroom. In Atwater, it lands in classrooms and at kitchen tables. In his account, a counselor is fired seven days after a public post. Families ask who speaks for their kids on Monday morning. Teachers cover the gap, parents hear the rumor before the record, and trust gets rebuilt one honest conversation at a time. That is why the record matters here, not the rumor.

How a district decision lands in Atwater. Follow @atwatercastleintelligence.

posts.title: They have 10 days to answer.
posts.caption:
They have 10 days to answer.

File a records request in California and the agency owes you a written determination in 10 days: do the records exist, and will they release them. An extension is allowed once, with a reason in writing.

Mark day 10. If nothing arrives, follow up in writing and ask for the determination by name.

Full how-to in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio, free. #MercedCounty #PublicAudit #209Media #California

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: Leadership After
posts.caption: LEADERSHIP AFTER. Getting fired does not end the leadership test. It starts a different one. A leader who loses the room has to decide what he carries next. He kept the ledger, he kept the receipts, and he kept showing up for the work. The next job is not revenge. It is building something that outlasts the room that cut you out. Document the decision, name the standard, and let the next room be one you built on purpose. What a leader does next. Follow @davidsicairos_.

posts.title: ILLEGALLY FIRED: The Paper Trail
posts.caption: THE PAPER TRAIL. The paper trail starts with two dates. September 11, 2025, a public post names him and his workplace. September 18, the district fires him, and the letter gives no reason. Between those dates, the record shows calls flooding the district office. What the file does not show matters too. No documented warning, no documented process, and no reason in writing. That gap is not a verdict. It is the question the records still have to answer, and the audit keeps asking it. His account, told through documents only. Follow 209Connect California.

posts.title: Ask for the record, not the answer.
posts.caption:
Ask for the record, not the answer.

When you file a public records request, name the document you want. A date range, a subject, and the office that holds it. That is what makes a request searchable. Vague questions get vague answers, but a named record creates a deadline the agency has to meet.

Start with one record. Get it back. Then ask for the next one.

Full how-to in the 209connect newsletter, link in bio, free. #MercedCounty #PublicAudit #209Media
